title: Conceal, Reconstruct, Jailbreak: Exploiting the Reconstruction--Concealment Tradeoff in MLLMs
claim: A staged pipeline builds concealed multimodal inputs from a query, with an optional side module adding related distractors, to bypass safety.
layout: Top left-to-right pipeline row, lower dashed sub-module, right distractor image panel
description: A wide, mostly left-to-right flow diagram. The top row starts with a gray 'Harmful query' box. It feeds pink boxes for character-removed candidate pool and concealment-aware variant selection, then a teal strategy-specific input construction box that lists TxtV, TxtV-GDI, TypV, TTV and TTV-GDI. Next come a pink victim MLLM box and an orange judging and metrics box. Colored section headers (§3.1, §3.2, attack execution) sit above the boxes. Dashed gray arrows lead down to a selected-variant-set box and a model-response example. A lower dashed purple module has four blue boxes: keyword/phrase, diverse sentence generation, related image generation and distractor-image selection. A dotted blue line carries the keyword w from the query into this module. The module feeds a right-hand panel with a 3x3 grid of real distractor photos. A dotted arrow runs from the module back up to the strategy box.
caption: Overview of the proposed reconstruction-based jailbreak framework. Starting from a harmful query xt, character-removed candidates are constructed and a diverse, low-keyword/phrasealignment subset ˆV(xt) is selected (§3.1), then instantiated through one of five prompting strategies that distribute the transformed information across text and image modalities (§3.2). For GDI-based strategies (TxtV-GDI, TTV-GDI), keyword/phrase-related distractor images D(xt) are additionally constructed from the harmful keyword/phrase w and composed into the visual input (§3.3). The resulting multimodal input (ˆxt, ˆxv) is passed to the victim MLLM Fθ and evaluated by a judge model.
abstract: Intent-obfuscation-based jailbreak attacks on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) transform a harmful query into a concealed multimodal input to bypass safety mechanisms. We study these attacks through the lens of a reconstruction-concealment tradeoff: the transformed input must sufficiently obscure harmful intent while preserving enough information for the victim model to recover the underlying request. Through a reconstruction and concealment analysis of representative black-box methods, we find that existing transformations struggle to balance this tradeoff, limiting their effectiveness. In contrast, we show that character-removed variants, constructed by randomly removing characters from the original query, achieve a better balance, motivating their use as the basis for our attack construction. Building on this observation, we propose concealment-aware variant construction, which selects character-removed variants with low harmful keyword/phrase alignment and high mutual diversity, and instantiates them through five prompting strategies that distribute the transformed information across text and image channels. We further introduce keyword/phrase-related distractor images that depict the harmful concept in diverse contexts, providing more effective distraction than generic distractor images. Experiments across diverse closed-source and open-source MLLMs show that the proposed strategies substantially outperform the evaluated baselines. Code and reproduction instructions are available at https://github.com/Farhamdur/CRJ.
